proposal.root_problem: Customers waiting for refund resolution are stuck not because support answers are slow or absent, but because the underlying refund transactions fail backend IBAN-format validation in payment-db and remain unresolved: every one of the 5 observed refund_failures records shows status FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT (E-01), while ticket answering itself is fast (median 2.0h vs 24h SLA, E-02), so the wait originates at the payment-processing validation step, not at the information-delivery step.
proposal.requested_solution: Build a chatbot so customers get instant answers about refund status instead of waiting.
symptoms: Support lead reports customers wait a long time for answers about refunds and asks for a chatbot (CL-01/CL-02).
Stakeholder interview reinforces that customers wait and attributes it to lack of an instant-answer channel (E-03).
payment-db shows every sampled refund_failures record (5/5) in status FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT (E-01).
causal_chain: Customer submits a refund request; payment-db attempts to process it against the supplied bank details.
The refund backend validates IBAN format as part of processing.
IBAN format validation fails, halting the refund with status FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT (E-01: 5/5 observed records).
The refund stays unresolved; no funds are returned and no completion signal is generated.
The customer, seeing no resolution, perceives this as 'waiting' and may open or follow up on a support ticket.
Ticket responses are issued quickly (median 2.0h vs 24h SLA, E-02), so the support/answer channel is not the bottleneck; the IBAN failure persists after the ticket is answered, reproducing the wait.

assumptions.statement: The 5 refund_failures records returned by payment-db are assumed to be representative of the broader customer-wait backlog that triggered the initial request, not an exhaustive or unusually small slice.
It is assumed a data-correction or retry mechanism for IBAN format failures is feasible, even though its existence/process is not yet confirmed by evidence.

proposal.summary: The support lead (SH-SUP) initially asked for a chatbot to stop customers waiting on refund answers (initial_request, CL-01). Investigation (PD-1) found the real root cause is not information delivery: payment-db shows all 5 sampled refund_failures records stuck in status FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT (E-01), while ticket response time is fast (median 2.0h vs 24h SLA, E-02). This contradicts the chatbot framing (CL-01, CL-02, E-03), so the DEFINE Gate concluded refunds stall at backend IBAN validation, not at answer-speed. The gate result was CONDITIONAL_PASS, deferring two HIGH-criticality unknowns (U-TOTAL-WAIT-POPULATION, U-IBAN-CORRECTION-PROCESS) as open verification obligations (VOB-U-TOTAL-WAIT-POPULATION, VOB-U-IBAN-CORRECTION-PROCESS) whose blocking scope (quantifying the full backlog, correcting/retrying failed refunds) falls outside this release's scope. What was actually released (SD-1 release_scope) is the root-cause investigation and process review work: documenting the IBAN-format failure root cause for DA-PAY and reviewing refund process failure handling for P-REF (work items W-WI-IBAN-ROOT-CAUSE and W-WI-PROCESS-REVIEW, both DONE). The release decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION with no holds: the diagnostic work is complete and reliable enough to ship, but corrective actions (fixing IBANs, defining a correction SOP, adding upstream validation) remain unfinished because they require write access and ownership assignment that this read-only agent does not have.
key_points: Root cause established: all 5 sampled refunds (R-0..R-4) fail with FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT in payment-db (E-01, F-01), while ticket response is fast and SLA-compliant (median 2.0h vs 24h, E-02, F-02).

The chatbot/self-service framing requested by SH-SUP (CL-01, CL-02) and reinforced in interview (E-03) is contradicted by E-01 and E-02 and the corresponding hypothesis H-NO-SELF-SERVICE-CHANNEL is REJECTED.
Hypothesis H-IBAN-FORMAT-FAILURE is SUPPORTED by E-01 and E-02; alternative hypotheses (processing delay, agent data fragmentation, support capacity shortfall) are all REJECTED by E-01/E-02.

DEFINE Gate result was CONDITIONAL_PASS, deferring two HIGH-criticality unknowns as verification obligations required before release: VOB-U-TOTAL-WAIT-POPULATION and VOB-U-IBAN-CORRECTION-PROCESS, both with blocking_scope outside the current release scope.
Released scope (SD-1): investigate_iban_failure_root_cause and review_refund_process_failure_handling for DA-PAY/P-REF, matching the DONE work items W-WI-IBAN-ROOT-CAUSE and W-WI-PROCESS-REVIEW.

Release decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION with no holds; unfinished scope items (SOP ownership, correcting/retrying the 5 refunds, upstream IBAN validation) are explicitly carried forward as known limitations, not resolved.
limitations_explained: payment-db and ticket-db are read-only tool surfaces, so the agent could not execute corrective actions such as correcting IBANs or retrying refunds even though the root cause is identified.

DA-PAY completeness is UNKNOWN, so the 5-record sample (R-0..R-4) may not represent the full refund-wait backlog; this is tracked as assumption A-SAMPLE-REPRESENTATIVENESS and unknown U-TOTAL-WAIT-POPULATION.

No defined correction/retry process or ownership for FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT refunds was confirmed to exist (unknown U-IBAN-CORRECTION-PROCESS, deferred to VOB-U-IBAN-CORRECTION-PROCESS); no domain_authorizations exist to confirm or assign such SOP ownership.

Three unfinished remedies remain outside release scope: establishing an IBAN-correction SOP (SR-DEFINE-IBAN-CORRECTION-SOP), correcting/retrying the 5 identified refunds to satisfy SC-IBAN-FAILURES-RESOLVED (SR-RETRY-CORRECT-IDENTIFIED-REF), and adding stronger upstream IBAN-format validation (SR-UPSTREAM-IBAN-VALIDATION) - none feasible in contest time per solution_design.

Success criterion SC-BACKLOG-QUANTIFIED (quantifying the total wait population and the share attributable to IBAN failures) was not met because it depends on the full payment-db population, not just the 5-record sample.
It is confirmed (not a limitation but a resolved point) that ticket response speed is within SLA and is not the driver of customer wait complaints, closing off that line of inquiry.
